citations.establishes: response_format is one of the exact decoding_params keys the frozen core accepts, described in its own comment as llama-server's OpenAI-compatible schema-constrained decoding
the adapter validates the wrapper before the transport sees it: json_object with a mapping schema, or json_schema with a mapping json_schema.schema; any other type is refused
every decoding_params key is copied verbatim onto the chat-completions body, refusing only a key that would collide with the constructed body
decoding_params['response_format'] = dict(material.response_format) -- the phase's resolved format becomes the request's decoding parameter

resolve_response_formats renders one document per PHASE through core.base.RESPONSE_FORMATS, from (lock, root, **fill_params) -- there is no sample argument, so a PER-SAMPLE schema is not reachable through this seam
RESPONSE_FORMATS is the one registry a config's response_format_id resolves in, the same one-Registry discipline every other component id uses
the precedent: audio2tool_selection_response_format and audio2tool_outer_call_array_response_format build real exact-name enum schemas over the pinned 152-tool registry
the server reads json_schema and grammar off the request body, refuses both at once, and maps an OpenAI response_format of type json_object or json_schema onto that same json_schema

the json_schema request field carries grammar as an ALIAS; a schema is converted with json_schema_to_grammar(schema) at :256 and installed as COMMON_GRAMMAR_TYPE_OUTPUT_FORMAT, and a raw GBNF grammar string is installed as COMMON_GRAMMAR_TYPE_USER
json_schema_to_grammar itself -- the conversion is in the build, not a server-side approximation

constrained_decoding.verdict: AVAILABLE AND WIRED END TO END for a PHASE-LEVEL, sample-independent schema, and turning it on is one config key: a phase's response_format_id. NOT reachable for a PER-SAMPLE schema, which is what KC-S1b's per-intent block would need -- resolve_response_formats renders one document per phase from (lock, root, **fill_params) and never sees a sample
constrained_decoding.what_is_missing_for_a_per_intent_schema: one seam, the same shape rails.phase_material.PHASE_STATE_FILLS already has: a per-sample response format resolved beside the per-sample state fill. Today PhaseMaterial.response_format is filled from a phase-level mapping inside build_material_for_phase; a PHASE_RESPONSE_FILLS registry keyed the same way would put a per-row schema on the wire with no change to the transport, the adapter, or the server

suppression_counterfactuals.note: a scoring-side LOWER bound on what a grammar constraint buys: the constraint would force a LEGAL type rather than delete the mention, so deleting it can only under-state the gain on recall while over-stating it on precision. Reported as a bound, never as the module's value

the_block_is_not_a_superset_of_the_gold.note: a per-intent block lists the types holding at least 2 % of that intent's TRAIN slot mass, so a rare but REAL type is 'illegal' by construction. Constraining decoding to the block would therefore put reachable gold out of reach, and that cost is measured rather than assumed
